title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: NATE ON THE ICE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Nate, a dog groomer from Toledo, Ohio.
He bathes poodles. He has never been cold on purpose.
Then Grandpa handed him the key to an old ice fishing shack.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE FIRST STEP
segments.quote: Only those who will risk going too far can possibly find out how far one can go.
segments.author: T. S. Eliot
lines: Grandpa's knees were done, so he sent Nate to the Lake Erie walleye derby with his buddy Stan.
Nate heard the ice groan and froze.
Taped inside the shack door was a line from T. S. Eliot:
Only those who will risk going too far can possibly find out how far one can go.
Stan said, eight inches, solid. Nate took one step. Then a hundred.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE EXPERT
segments.quote: Angling may be said to be so like the mathematics, that it can never be fully learnt.
segments.author: Izaak Walton
lines: Nate figured fishing was easy. Hole, line, fish, done.
Two Saturdays later, he had caught one glove and a cold.
Stan showed him a line from Izaak Walton, an old English writer:
Angling may be said to be so like the mathematics, that it can never be fully learnt.
So Nate stopped pretending and asked questions.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: EMPTY BUCKET
segments.quote: Hope is a good breakfast, but it is a bad supper.
segments.author: Francis Bacon
lines: Every morning, Nate drove out full of hope. Every night, an empty bucket.
Grandpa read him a line from Francis Bacon over the phone:
Hope is a good breakfast, but it is a bad supper.
So Nate made a plan. A notebook. Depth, bait, wind.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: GRUMPY DUANE
segments.quote: The only way you can make a man trustworthy is to trust him.
segments.author: Henry L. Stimson
lines: Next to them fished Duane, who never said hello.
One morning, Duane's ice drill died. Too proud to ask.
Nate remembered Henry Stimson, an old Secretary of War:
The only way you can make a man trustworthy is to trust him.
He handed Duane his drill. The next day, Duane showed him where the walleye hide.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: DERBY DAY
segments.quote: Luck affects everything. Let your hook always be cast. In the stream where you least expect it, there will be a fish.
segments.author: Ovid
lines: Derby day. Three hours. Nothing.
Nate wanted to pack up. Stan quoted Ovid, a poet from ancient Rome:
Luck affects everything. Let your hook always be cast. In the stream where you least expect it, there will be a fish.
So Nate dropped a second line in a shallow hole nobody tried.
Right before the horn, the rod bent double. An eight-pound walleye.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE SLED
segments.quote: It is the sweet, simple things of life which are the real ones after all.
segments.author: Laura Ingalls Wilder
lines: Nate took fourth place. No trophy. Just a hat.
Next weekend, he pulled Grandpa onto the ice on a sled, wrapped like a burrito.
In the warm shack, Grandpa caught the first fish. Stan quoted Laura Ingalls Wilder:
It is the sweet, simple things of life which are the real ones after all.
Nate wore that hat all spring.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Take the step. Stay humble. Make a plan. Trust first. Keep your hook in. Enjoy the simple things.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Take the step. Stay humble. Make a plan. Trust first. Keep your hook in. Enjoy the simple things.
I went ice fishing once. All I caught was a nap.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
